description: Django REST Framework serializer makes 847 SQL queries on a list endpoint with 50 items. Each item has a reverse ForeignKey to Comments (avg 12 per item) and each Comment has a ForeignKey to User. The ViewSet uses ModelSerializer with depth=2. Adding prefetch_related('comments') reduced queries to 52 but User still causes N+1. Need to reduce to 3 queries total.
expectedSolution: Use nested prefetch: prefetch_related(Prefetch('comments', queryset=Comment.objects.select_related('user'))). The Prefetch object allows attaching select_related to the inner queryset.

description: React app with AuthContext provider causes every component in the tree to re-render when the auth token refreshes every 5 minutes, even components that only use user.name (not the token). Performance profiler shows 200+ unnecessary re-renders on token refresh. useMemo on context value doesn't help because the object reference changes.
expectedSolution: Split AuthContext into two separate contexts: AuthTokenContext (changes on refresh) and UserContext (changes on login/logout). Components consuming only user data won't re-render on token refresh. Alternative: use a state management library with selectors like zustand.

description: Node.js Transform stream processes CSV records in parallel using async operations (database lookups). Output CSV has records in random order instead of preserving input order. Using highWaterMark=64 for throughput. Switching to objectMode didn't help. Records must maintain original order while keeping parallel processing for performance.
expectedSolution: Buffer results with sequence numbers: assign index on read, process in parallel, buffer output until next expected index arrives. Or use a parallel-transform library that maintains order. Or collect into array, Promise.all, then write sequentially.

description: Prisma transaction intermittently fails with P2034 'Transaction already closed' when two concurrent requests try to update the same user's balance. Using $transaction with interactive mode. Retry logic causes duplicate deductions. The balance can go negative which violates business rules. Need atomic balance update with proper isolation.
expectedSolution: Use optimistic locking: add a version field, UPDATE users SET balance = balance - amount, version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ? AND balance >= amount. Check affected rows = 1. Or use raw SQL with SELECT FOR UPDATE in serializable transaction.

description: Next.js 14 App Router: passing a Date object from Server Component to Client Component causes 'Only plain objects can be passed to Client Components from Server Components' error. Converting to string loses timezone info. The component needs both server-side data fetching and client-side date formatting with user's locale. Workaround with JSON.stringify loses the Date prototype methods.
expectedSolution: Pass dates as ISO strings (date.toISOString()) from Server Component, reconstruct with new Date(isoString) in Client Component. For complex serialization use superjson. The client-side Date constructor preserves timezone handling with Intl.DateTimeFormat for locale formatting.

description: FastAPI endpoint hangs indefinitely when calling an async function that internally uses asyncio.run() to call another async function. Works fine when called directly but deadlocks when called from a FastAPI route handler. The inner function is from a third-party library that was designed for sync callers.
expectedSolution: asyncio.run() creates a new event loop but can't run inside an existing one. Use asyncio.to_thread() or loop.run_in_executor(None, sync_wrapper) to run the blocking call in a thread pool. Or use nest_asyncio.apply() as a quick fix. For production, refactor to use await directly.

description: TypeScript utility type that should extract all nullable properties from an interface returns 'never' for optional properties. type NullableKeys<T> = { [K in keyof T]: null extends T[K] ? K : never }[keyof T] doesn't match properties declared as 'name?: string' because optional properties have type 'string | undefined' not 'string | null'. Need to handle both optional (undefined) and nullable (null) properties.
expectedSolution: Use: type OptionalKeys<T> = { [K in keyof T]-?: {} extends Pick<T, K> ? K : never }[keyof T]. The -? removes optionality for the check. {} extends Pick<T, K> is true only when K is optional. For nullable: type NullableKeys<T> = { [K in keyof T]: null extends T[K] ? K : undefined extends T[K] ? K : never }[keyof T].

description: Kubernetes pods are being OOMKilled despite container memory limit set to 2Gi and application heap set to 1.5Gi (-Xmx1536m for Java). kubectl top shows pod using 1.8Gi. The JVM uses memory outside the heap (metaspace, thread stacks, native buffers, GC overhead). Container memory limit doesn't account for non-heap JVM memory.
expectedSolution: Set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 instead of fixed -Xmx to leave room for non-heap. Or increase container limit to 2.5Gi. Enable -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary to audit. Account for: metaspace (~256MB), thread stacks (1MB × threads), direct buffers, GC overhead (~15% of heap).

description: GraphQL resolver using DataLoader batches requests across different user sessions — User A sees User B's private data. The DataLoader instance is created once at server start and shared across all requests. Caching behavior means the first resolver to load an entity wins, and subsequent requests for the same ID get the cached (possibly unauthorized) result.
expectedSolution: Create a new DataLoader instance per request in the GraphQL context factory: context: ({ req }) => ({ loaders: { userLoader: new DataLoader(batchUsers) } }). DataLoaders must be request-scoped, never shared across requests. Clear the cache after mutations.

description: Rust borrow checker error: closure may outlive the current function, but it borrows `config` which is owned by the current function. The closure is passed to a thread::spawn. Moving config into the closure with move || works but then config can't be used after spawn. Need to share config across multiple spawned threads.
expectedSolution: Wrap config in Arc<T> for shared ownership: let config = Arc::new(config); For each thread: let config = Arc::clone(&config); thread::spawn(move || { /* use config */ }). If mutation needed, use Arc<Mutex<T>> or Arc<RwLock<T>>.

description: Webpack 5 build produces circular chunk dependencies causing runtime error: 'Loading chunk X failed'. Two lazy-loaded routes import from a shared barrel file that re-exports from both route modules. Splitting with optimization.splitChunks doesn't resolve because the barrel file creates a bidirectional dependency. Code splitting is broken.
expectedSolution: Remove the barrel file re-exports that create circular dependencies. Import directly from the source module instead of through the barrel: import { X } from './featureA/component' not from './features'. Mark package.json sideEffects: false to enable tree-shaking. Use webpack-bundle-analyzer to verify chunk boundaries.

description: PostgreSQL query SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24h' takes 12 seconds on 50M row table. B-tree index on (status, created_at) exists but EXPLAIN shows sequential scan. The index has 50M entries but only 0.1% of orders are 'pending'. The query planner chooses seqscan because index statistics show the combined columns aren't selective enough.
expectedSolution: Create a partial index: CREATE INDEX idx_pending_orders ON orders(created_at) WHERE status = 'pending'. This index only contains the ~50K pending rows, making it tiny and fast. Run ANALYZE afterwards. The partial index is orders of magnitude smaller than the full index.

description: Docker multi-stage build takes 8 minutes because npm ci runs on every code change even though package.json didn't change. The Dockerfile copies everything first then runs install. Layer caching is invalidated by any source file change. Need to optimize so dependency install only reruns when package.json changes.
expectedSolution: Copy package files first, install, then copy source: COPY package*.json ./ → RUN npm ci → COPY . . Docker caches layers sequentially — if package.json hasn't changed, npm ci layer is cached. Use .dockerignore to exclude node_modules.

description: Celery tasks disappear after worker restart — no retry, no error, just gone. Using Redis broker with visibility_timeout=3600. Long-running tasks (>1h) get redelivered to another worker while still executing on the first, causing duplicate processing. Acking early loses at-least-once guarantee. Acking late causes the redelivery.
expectedSolution: Set task_acks_late=True with task_reject_on_worker_lost=True. Increase visibility_timeout beyond max task duration. Make tasks idempotent (safe to run twice). Use task_time_limit to kill stuck tasks. For very long tasks, implement periodic heartbeat that extends the visibility timeout.

description: React Suspense with multiple data-fetching components creates a waterfall — Component B doesn't start fetching until Component A's data resolves and renders. Each component uses useSuspenseQuery independently. Total load time is sum of all fetches instead of max. React.Suspense boundary wraps the parent, showing one loading state.
expectedSolution: Preload all queries at the router level before rendering: start all fetches in parallel in a route loader or parent component, then pass promises down. Use render-as-you-fetch pattern: const promise = fetchData(); function Component() { const data = use(promise); }. Or use React Router's loader/defer.

description: Python metaclass-based plugin registry doesn't discover plugins in subpackages. The registry uses __init_subclass__ to auto-register. Plugins in app/plugins/auth/handler.py are not registered because Python doesn't import submodules automatically. importlib.import_module with wildcard doesn't work. Need automatic discovery of all plugin classes across nested packages.
expectedSolution: Use pkgutil.walk_packages to recursively discover and import all submodules: for importer, modname, ispkg in pkgutil.walk_packages(package.__path__, package.__name__ + '.'): importlib.import_module(modname). Call this at app startup. Alternatively, use setuptools entry_points for plugin discovery.

description: Go HTTP server leaks goroutines — pprof shows goroutine count growing by ~100/hour. Each request spawns a goroutine that reads from a channel, but if the request context is cancelled (client disconnects), the goroutine blocks forever on channel read. select with ctx.Done() is used but the producer goroutine also leaks because nobody reads from the channel after consumer exits.
expectedSolution: Use buffered channel so producer doesn't block if consumer exits. Add select with ctx.Done() on BOTH producer and consumer sides. Use defer cancel() to ensure context cancellation propagates. Consider errgroup for coordinated goroutine lifecycle management.

description: CSS Grid layout collapses to zero height when child elements are positioned with position: absolute. The grid container has grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto but the 1fr row collapses because absolutely positioned children are removed from flow. Switching to relative positioning breaks the overlay design. Need grid sizing to work while allowing absolute positioning for overlapping elements.
expectedSolution: Instead of position: absolute, use CSS Grid's native overlap: place both elements in the same grid-area (grid-row: 1/2; grid-column: 1/2) and control stacking with z-index. The grid cell sizes to the content of both elements. Or set explicit min-height on the grid container.

description: JWT verification passes for tokens signed with an RSA public key as HMAC secret. The verify function accepts both HS256 and RS256 algorithms. An attacker takes the public RS256 key (publicly available), uses it as the HMAC secret to forge a token with alg: HS256, and the server accepts it because the same key material verifies both.
expectedSolution: Always specify the exact expected algorithm in verify options: jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] }). Never allow the token's alg header to determine the verification algorithm. This is the JWT algorithm confusion attack (CVE-2016-5431). Pin the algorithm on the server side.

description: Redis cache stampede: when a popular cache key expires, 500 concurrent requests all miss cache simultaneously, all hit the database, all write back to cache. Database CPU spikes to 100%. Simple TTL-based caching with cache-aside pattern. Need to prevent the thundering herd while keeping data fresh.
expectedSolution: Use distributed lock (SETNX) so only one request rebuilds the cache: if cache miss, try SETNX lock_key → if acquired, rebuild and cache → release lock; if not acquired, wait briefly and retry cache read. Alternative: stale-while-revalidate — serve stale data while one request refreshes in background. Add jitter to TTLs to prevent synchronized expiry.
